milestones.name: Coherent contract and substrate qualification
exit_criteria: Current requirements retain every legacy ID with explicit amendments and owned integration gaps.
Pinned local Appwrite primitives and their limits are recorded; remaining adapter/domain proof is named.
Next-tranche tasks have source contracts and native dependency relations; historical cuts/estimates do not release work.

milestones.name: Scoped resource, identity and action kernel
exit_criteria: Appwrite-native boundaries and indexed scope/ID mapping pass domain/provider contracts.
Individual identity/membership and narrow standing delegation enforce the same scope through UI/API discovery.
Resources, capabilities, action plans, operations and authorized event/read contracts are usable in the replica.

milestones.name: One project control surface over current owners
exit_criteria: A colleague and delegated agent inspect a task, policy, run and delivery evidence through canonical links.
Policy reads and supported writes route to the owner with lifecycle and attribution; unsupported writer scope stays explicit.
Archetype/role/skill/context/version adoption, graph, grooming queue and triage are manageable without competing source writers.

milestones.name: Bound native execution
exit_criteria: Bindings pin required context/skills/workflows and resource/credential envelope.
Concurrent claims, recovery, stage isolation and lease fencing work against the qualified persistence boundary.
A scripted complete chain executes through the native engine in the local replica.

milestones.name: Governed native delivery
exit_criteria: Required review/checks, conflict handling and landing use the source host native gate with no inferred admin bypass.
Delivery observations distinguish merge, publication, desired/reconciled revision and health with freshness.
Release requests follow existing reviewed CI/GitOps; no product-shell deployment or custom restore controller.

milestones.name: Owned unattended operation
exit_criteria: Each stall/triage class has bounded attempts, owner, observed repair and declared exit.
Grooming is serialized per project and independently observed mechanisms report stale/unknown honestly.
Notifications/acknowledgement escalate through the actual owner/goal chain under standing authority.

milestones.name: Measured improvement and portfolio operation
exit_criteria: One ranked candidate is pursued once, linked to Closer work, landed and explicitly adopted.
A binding/run proves usage and outcome evidence retains coverage/confounders; merge alone is not effectiveness.
Portfolio/concierge/knowledge/experiment views use the same authorized objects and partner capability status.

milestones.name: Qualified project and resource-family handovers
exit_criteria: Each selected project/family has complete snapshot/provenance, matched behavior and one fenced writer.
Full policy-history/variant/import snapshot is required only if that policy family actually migrates.
Rollback/retirement is scoped to accepted owners/consumers; unmigrated meta-harness/Plane and external products remain authoritative.

milestones.name: Independent installation and distribution
exit_criteria: A documented private self-hosted installation connects to a supported Appwrite substrate without estate-only assumptions.
Upgrade, recovery, supply-chain and access boundaries are exercised in the local replica.
Public naming/licensing/publication or independent-tenant activation retains its explicit authority and isolation acceptance; none is implied by a colleague invitation.

rules: Board state is authoritative; no calendar/lane-time/task-count estimates.
Packages are requirement groupings, not single-PR tasks.
Decompose only next tranche; <=3 named acceptance tests per feature slice.
Cross-project capability needs are explicit source contracts and owner work, never prose gates.
MS6 can start after MS2 through the current execution adapter; it need not wait for full engine replacement.
Private collaborator pilot does not require every legacy project migration or public release.

technical_review.scope: requirements and planned contracts; not runtime implementation
